content.title: How Rory McIlroy won Masters 2026 to become fourth man to defend title
content.text: McIlroy wins second straight MastersRory McIlroy has won the Masters for the second straight year, shooting a final-round 71 to finish at 12 under par, one stroke better than runner-up Scottie Scheffler. A dramatic final round saw Cameron Young, who began the day with a share of the lead, and Justin Rose both lead by two strokes at separate points, but neither could keep pace on the back nine. McIlroy is just the fourth golfer to win back-to-back Masters tournaments, joining Jack Nicklaus (1965-66), Nick Faldo (1989-90) and Tiger Woods (2001-02). This is the sixth major championship for the golfer from Northern Ireland. Share your reaction with us at live@theathletic.com. WinnerPOSPLAYERTOTAL1Rory McIlroyNIR-12SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementCan McIlroy get to 10 majors? Getty ImagesThis Q&A from our Alex Kirshner and Gabby Herzig is part of our Golf Briefing newsletter on Rory McIlroy's win at the Masters:Alex: That's six majors and two green jackets. He's won a road Ryder Cup. The Grand Slam was already in the bag. I don't sense that Rory will ever have a complacency problem, but how would you even judge success for him over the next, say, five years of his career? Gabby: McIlroy just talked about this in his news conference. It sounds like he originally thought that winning the Grand Slam would provide him the ultimate satisfaction, but it didn’t. And I interpret that to mean that McIlroy is about to put his foot on the gas in majors. I’d dare to say that McIlroy is chasing double digits in his major count. Maybe that won’t happen in the next five or six years, but it doesn’t feel out of the question at all for McIlroy’s career as a whole.Which shot stands out? Getty ImagesThis Q&A from our Alex Kirshner and Gabby Herzig is part of our Golf Briefing newsletter on Rory McIlroy's win at the Masters:Alex: You watched perhaps thousands of golf shots. Which one that you saw in person will stick with you the longest?Gabby: Honestly, this sounds counterintuitive, but I think the two out-of-sorts golf shots I saw McIlroy hit on both No. 11 and No. 12 with irons yesterday will stick with me the most from this tournament. For years, McIlroy has been telling the media that he will really know that he’s reached elite levels of the game if he is able to win tournaments without his best stuff. And this week, he did not have that — especially off the tee. Even after Sunday’s round, where he started to swing a little bit more freely, McIlroy was ranked No. 53 out of 54 in driving accuracy for the entire week, and he still won the Masters. It’s an absurd statement, especially knowing that the strength of McIlroy’s game are his tee shots. His gritty short game and putting held things up for him all week, and it paid off.During his winner’s news conference, I actually asked him to grade his play: He gave his driving a B-, his irons a B and his short game and putting an A+.How was this year different? Getty ImagesThis Q&A from our Alex Kirshner and Gabby Herzig is part of our Golf Briefing newsletter on Rory McIlroy's win at the Masters:Alex: To what extent did watching McIlroy this week feel different than watching him here every other year? Was the crowd more receptive to someone else winning? Were you more confident that he wouldn't let this thing get away from him?Gabby: It felt different, because the stakes objectively weren’t as high for him. He wasn’t chasing that one last win, he no longer “needed” the career Grand Slam. So he could breathe. Even after he let a six-shot 36-hole lead disappear, there was less on the line. You could see how that impacted him from a confidence standpoint, and other players took note of it. Freddie Couples even said, “Rory might never lose this things again.”But that did not mean his actual golf was any less stressful to watch. I was out there as the crowds swung with emotion yesterday. McIlroy is so human and so relatable in the way that you never know he’s going to do next. There were definitely a few people out there rooting for Justin Rose, but generally, McIlroy is the crowd pleaser because he makes things entertaining in a beautiful way.How sportsbooks reacted to McIlroy's win Multiple sportsbooks were happy with Rory McIlroy winning the 2026 Masters. Before the event began, McIlroy's odds to win his second green jacket were in the range of 11-1 to 14-1, depending on the sportsbook."Rory [McIlroy] was a very good result for the book as support for him was tempered pre-tournament," VP of risk management at the Westgate Sportsbook, Jeff Sherman, told The Athletic.Borgata Sportsbook director Thomas Gable shared similar sentiments, 💬 "Rory (McIlroy) winning that green jacket was the best outcome for us in terms of the pre-tournament outright winner market."McIlroy makes more history Getty ImagesRory McIlroy made history for the second straight year at Augusta National. Last year, it was earning the career Grand Slam. This year, it's becoming the fourth player to repeat as the Masters champion.Our Gabby Herzig has the story on McIlroy's win here. SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementAggressive mindset pays off Rory McIlroy said he got defensive last year on the 13th hole in the final round, and that hurt him. He said he stayed aggressive today on the 12th and 13th holes because of what happened last year.💬“Staying aggressive and staying committed, especially on those two holes, served me.”Let's hear from Scottie Scheffler After shooting a final-round 68, Scottie Scheffler spoke with CBS despite losing by one. 💬 “The first few days. I played what I was really solid on Thursday. Friday with the softer greens. That round really hurt.”“Over the weekend, I put up a good fight to give myself a chance. Just finished a couple shots shot.”Georgia natives to win the Masters Russell Henley got close today and likely had a real chance to win the Masters as a Georgia native. But the fact remains the same: Only three Georgia natives have won the Masters: Claude Harmon (Savannah, 1948), Tommy Aaron (Gainesville, 1973) and Larry Mize (Augusta, 1987).Another 'stinger' for Rose Justin Rose finished in the top 10 at the Masters for the eighth time, and that includes three runner-up finishes. He finished T3 this year at 10 under.And he received a terrific ovation from the spectators surrounding the 18th green.💬 “It was nice. I felt like the crowd was amazing to me all week long. They pulled for me all week long. I felt their encouragement and support. At the end, it kind of goes a little flat. It's more of a sympathy than anything.“But it was still, nonetheless, very beautiful. It’s another little stinger.”Schauffele is 'playing pretty nice' Xander Schauffele’s 2025 season was thrown off by a rib injury, but it seems like he is back to being himself health-wise. And his game has followed. Schauffele finished at 8 under and is tied for ninth.💬 “I feel like I played better than what I shot. Sometimes that's how golf goes. You need a few things to go your way, a few lip-out putts to lip in. But for the most part, I felt like I controlled my ball and wasn't in too many weird spots. Just struggled on the greens a little bit overall.“I've got something good coming around the corner here. I'm playing pretty nice.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementNot looking for chatter Getty ImagesA year ago Bryson DeChambeau was quite bothered by the lack of chatter between he and Rory McIlroy in the final group at the Masters. Cameron Young was ready for it and typical of his laid-back personality, not offended by it.“I mean, I'm not one to talk a ton to begin with, and I don't think he really be the wanted to talk to me today. Sunday at the Masters in the final group, you know, don't wish anything poorly on the guy, but we're playing against each other,” Young said. “Not trying to be best friends out there.“Just one of those times that either you leave each other be and if there is a moment — there were one or two but not many.”Young shot a 73 today to finish at 10 under par, in a four-way tie for third. It’s his best-ever finish at the Masters but still came up short of his hope for the day.“If you go through the back nine I pretty much had a birdie chance on every hole and didn't make any. That's how it goes sometimes,” Young said.Some crystal and a strong finish for Hatton Tyrrell Hatton shot his second 6-under 66 for the week today and finished at 10 under for his second top-10 Masters finish. He had an eagle and six birdies in the final round, including four straight birdies on the second nine.💬 “I'm really happy with the round that I put together in the end. Obviously, I had a nice run on the back nine.”The eagle came on the seventh hole when he holed out from the fairway with his approach. Players who score an eagle during the week receive a crystal prize from the club.💬 “The first thing is I shouted, crystal, which, yeah, obviously happy to make eagle. That's a huge bonus in the round, and, it helped me get a little bit of momentum.”Henley misses opportunities for more Russell Henley finished with six straight pars today, but he missed his chances on the green to claim his first major. The Georgia native finished at 10 under after a 68 today for his second top-10 Masters finish.💬 “I hit it amazing today. I gave myself a bunch of looks. Unfortunately, I didn't capitalize on those looks on the back, like I would have liked to.“I felt like I handled the pressure well, handled the conditions well. It was tricky out there. I just hit it great. I’m really thankful for a good finish. I wish I would have made some more putts and got a little closer to the lead, but overall, I’m very thankful.”Young felt like he handled the pressure Cameron Young finished in the top 10 at the Masters for the third time today with a T3 finish at 10 under. He shot a 1-over 73 today in the final round while playing with winner Rory McIlroy.💬 “I think I handled it fine; I just didn't make anything. That's the story of the week, honestly if you look through all four rounds. I had a chip in yesterday and maybe made a putt or two over 10 feet, and really that was it.“So I feel like I played the golf I needed to. I just didn't have the day making anything at all.”Rahm on his week Jon Rahm, a former Masters champion, finished the week at 1 over after rounds of 78-70-73-68. So what does he take from the week?💬 “Today was much better. Crazy, same person, right? Even though I made some mistakes I was able to rectify quite a few of them and have a good round. “I'll say it again, a lot of what not to do. I played really bad the two days. Shot 2-under on the second round but that was about as good as I should have shot with how I was hitting it.”SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementScheffler critiques Masters' Friday setup Scottie Scheffler made it quite clear after his round that he's pleased with the way he fought this weekend to give himself a chance, but disappointed at how Friday went for reasons in and out of his control.He was in the Thursday PM/Friday AM wave, shooting 70-74, and then watched Rory McIlroy shoot an afternoon 65 on Friday, and Cameron Young shoot a 67.💬 “I'm not in charge of course setup. I would have liked it to have been a little bit more equal in terms of the firmness on Thursday and Friday. I was a bit surprised at how soft things were on Friday afternoon, especially as it got late in the day.“But the weather also changes and it was a bit windy on Thursday, so who knows. That's part of the game.”Scottie was 12 back of McIlroy to start the weekend and ended up one shot back. “A pretty good run,” Scheffler said.Scheffler comes up just short Scottie Scheffler made a nice run this weekend in the Masters, but he couldn’t overcome the 74 he shot on Friday.Scheffler had rounds of 65-68 on the weekend, and had four birdies today. He finished second to Rory McIlroy, one shot back.💬 “The first two days I played what I felt was really solid on Thursday, and then Friday with the softer greens, that round really hurt, especially mistakes I made on the back nine. But overall over the weekend, I put up a good fight, did a lot of good stuff in order to give myself a chance and ultimately came up short.”McIlroy nets record prize money Not only does Rory McIlroy have another green jacket to slip into and another trophy for the mantlepiece, he also walks away with the biggest prize packet in major-championship history.Today's victory has earned him $4.5million in prize money, while second-placed Scottie Scheffler will pocket $2.43m.The first-place prize ties the Players Championship as the most lucrative payout in golf.What has McIlroy learned? Getty ImagesWhat has this tournament taught Rory McIlroy?💬 “Good things come to those who wait, maybe. Just keep going. I found myself in a very similar position today where I was last year, two or three behind. But I just played solid golf after that.”And what about having his parents there with him after they stayed at home last year?“I caught myself out on the golf course today thinking about them and thought, ‘No, not yet.’ But it was really cool to have them here.”One for the photo album Getty ImagesThere are so many great photos from this last week for Rory McIlroy, but I'm sure one will be one among his favorites.His father, Gerry, his mother, Rosie as well as his wife, Erica, and daughter, Poppy, were right there with him as he went to back-to-back.How precious.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMcIlroy: 'I still have things I want to achieve' Getty ImagesRory McIlroy was asked how he feels differently this year compared to last year, and how he will react to this one:💬 “Last year, I thought winning the career Grand Slam was the finish line, and I was wrong. ... I don’t want to put a number on it, but I feel like this win is just a part of the journey.“I still have things I want to achieve. I still want to enjoy it as well. I waited so long to win a Masters, and now I’ve won two straight.”A final word from McIlroy's green-jacket ceremony Getty ImagesAnd here was Rory McIlroy's closing remark.💬 “The Masters tournament continues to be the shining light of tournament golf and the majors. It's absolutely incredible. I'm so honored and so thrilled to be able to win this tournament for a second time and I can't wait to come back next year in 2027 and for many, many years to come.”A few words from McIlroy for his family Getty ImagesThen it was time for Rory McIlroy to get a little choked up as he thanked the four members of his family that greeted him after he walked off the 18th green.💬 “This is the hard part, I want to say a few thank yous to the people on my left. First and foremost my wife and daughter, Erica and Poppy. They have to put up with me at home and trust me, sometimes that's a tough thing for me to do. But they have been my biggest supporters and this has definitely turned into Poppy's favorite week of the year. I don't know if it's because of the Par 3 tournament or because of the all-you-can-eat ice cream in the player services building!“My mum and dad, they weren't here last year to celebrate with us and surprisingly I had to convince them to come this year. They thought that the reason I won was because they weren't here. I'm glad that we proved that wrong.“Mum and dad, I owe everything to you. You're the most wonderful parents and if I can be half the parent to Poppy as you were to me, then I know I've done a good job. Thank you.”McIlroy thanks the volunteers and the patronsA classy touch from Rory McIlroy to dedicate a special thank you the volunteers at Augusta National and the patrons who turned out to see him in their thousands this weekend.💬 “To the volunteers, I made you work overtime this week. I needed to clear a lot of patrons because I hit it in a lot of pine straw! So thank you for that and thank you for your continued support of the Masters tournament. This tournament wouldn't be the tournament it is without you guys, so thank you very much.To all the patrons, the support that I feel out there and the atmosphere that you all provide for the players to play in, it truly is a one-of-a-kind golf tournament. I said this last year but everyone is so present, so engaged in what's going on. As a player, it's a real privilege to play in that so thank you so much for that.”McIlroy not made to rue missing so many fairways Getty ImagesBest score to par when missing the fairway (par 4s and 5s), Masters champions since 2000:Hideki Matsuyama (2021): -6Rory McIlroy (2026): -5Phil Mickelson (2010): -5McIlroy’s 31 fairways hit are the fewest by a Masters champion in recorded history.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMcIlroy's on-course green-jacket ceremony Getty ImagesThere are no tears this time around for Rory McIlroy, just a smile as wide as the 18th fairway. Here is what he had to say at the on-course green-jacket ceremony.💬 “It still fits, which is nice. My parting message was 'I can't wait put the green jacket on myself'. I wasn't quite correct because the chairman did it, but I did want to come back here and prove that last year wasn't a fluke.“It is an absolutely incredible golf tournament. It is so unique in so many ways. There are a few people I want to thanks first and foremost. To chairman Ridley and everyone at Augusta National Golf Club, since I started to play this tournament you've really made me feel like one of your own and part of the club and for that I really want to say thank you.“I've always felt welcome here and I've built up such a great rapport with not only the members but the staff, and everyone on site that makes this experience absolutely incredible. So thank you to everyone involved.”Rory McIlroy looking to join another exclusive club Tiger Woods. Jack Nicklaus. Gary Player.Three of the greatest golfers of all time.They have won every major championship at least twice in their careers. Another win at the U.S. Open and Open Championship will see Rory McIlroy join that list.McIlroy’s lone U.S. Open came in 2011, his first major. His only Claret Jug was in 2014. Readers' thoughts on McIlroy Getty ImagesSome readers' thoughts on Rory McIlroy's second straight Masters winRick D: I don’t golf anymore because I’m older, but I wanna tell you it’s nice to see him win, thank youPhyllis T: Congratulations, RoryKatherine F: I believe he said in the Prime documentary that he wanted to make his four-year-old daughter proud.Alex W: The man is never dull, and maybe more fun than classic Tiger or Scottie.Today's top performers Today's leaderboard saw plenty of changes at the top, but in the end it was Rory McIlroy defending his Masters title. Which players saved their best performances for the final round and posted the best scores?Tyrrell Hatton: 66Keegan Bradley: 66Gary Woodland: 66Max Homa: 67Viktor Hovland: 67Maverick McNealy: 67McIlroy recorded a 71 and held on to win by a stroke.A week of two halves for McIlroy Getty ImagesAt no point this week did Rory McIlroy have his best golf but the run he put together on the back nine on Friday was electric and is the reason he is wearing the green jacket right now.That allowed him to dip a long way below his best today and yesterday, yet still have enough to get over the line. Though he did find a lot more accuracy with off the tee,Here is how his first two rounds compared with his second:-12 – Score to par – E15 – Birdies – 93 – Bogeys or worse – 746% – Fairways hit – 64%72% – Greens in reg. – 61%SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementRory McIlroy in the Masters ceremony: “I did want to come back here and prove last year wasn't a fluke.” Getty ImagesRory McIlroy is the first Masters champion in history to lose strokes to the field over the last 36 holes.The jacket 'still fits' Getty ImagesRory McIlroy opens his comments from the official green-jacket ceremony with a bit of a joke about the green jacket, saying, “It still fits.”Lots of laughs and cheers from the spectators. McIlroy glad to have a bigger cushion this year Getty ImagesRory McIlroy felt that this year’s final round at the Masters emulated 2025, where he completed the career Grand Slam. He spoke in Butler Cabin about what he needed to score to guarantee another green jacket. “Felt pretty similar to last year … I played flawless golf after that. “Four birdies no bogeys, going to the last tee. Nice to have that two-shot cushion instead of one last year. “I looked at the board and thought if I can get to 14 under I have a really good chance to win this tournament. 13 under was good enough.”What about three straight? Getty ImagesRory McIlroy will try to make even more history at the 2027 Masters as he looks to become the first player to win the tournament three years in a row.How did Jack Nicklaus, Nick Faldo and Tiger Woods fare in their bids for three straight?Jack Nicklaus (1967): Missed cutNick Faldo (1991): 24thTiger Woods (2003): T15SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementAn embrace between Faldo and McIlroyA lovely moment between Nick Faldo and Rory McIlroy as the latter exited Butler Cabin.The two multiple Masters champions shared a hug and a few words.Two of the four people who know how it feels to defend their crown here.Let's hear from Rory McIlroy in Butler Cabin Here is what Rory McIlroy had to say in Butler Cabin.“I can’t believe I waited 17 years to get the first green jacket. Now I've got two in a row. My perseverance at this golf tournament is starting to pay off.“I was so happy to hang in there and to get the job done.”McIlroy is given his second green jacket! Getty ImagesOver to Butler Cabin where Rory McIlroy has been chatting to Augusta National Golf Club chairman Fred Ridley and CBS host Jim Nantz.We'll have quotes from there very shortly but for now, the two-time champion has his second green jacket.As John mentioned a little earlier, with McIlroy being last year's winner too, it is the chairman's responsibility to hand him the jacket.McIlroy goes level as Europe’s greatest player Imagn ImagesThere have been some great players in the history of European golf. Seve Ballesteros, Nick Faldo, Bernhard Langer, just to name a few.But Rory McIlroy has gone level with Faldo and surpassed the rest, and he has plenty of his career to go in front of him.Anyone for the double Grand Slam?This time a year and a week ago, Rory McIlroy was still being asked whether he thought he could win the Grand Slam.Now, he has the chance to win each of the majors twice over.He needs another U.S. Open and Open Championship to double up.This year's U.S. Open will take place at Shinnecock Hills in June before the world's best golfers head to Royal Birkdale a month later for The Open.Before that, McIlroy will have a target on his back at next month's PGA Championship at Aronimink.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMcIlroy moves up all-time rankings Imagn ImagesRory McIlroy is just the 15th man to win at least six major championships in golf. 1. Jack Nicklaus - 182. Tiger Woods - 153. Walter Hagen - 11T4. Ben Hogan - 9T4. Gary Player - 96. Tom Watson - 8T7. Harry Vardon - 7T7 - Bobby Jones - 7T7. Gene Sarazen - 7T7. Sam Snead - 7T7. Arnold Palmer - 7T12. Rory McIlroy - 6T12. Lee Trevino - 6T12. Nick Faldo - 6T12. Phil Mickelson - 6McIlroy matches Faldo with six majorsRory McIlroy has joined Nick Faldo as the most successful European player in the modern era, with six major championships.These are the six he has racked up so far:U.S. Open 2011The Open 2014PGA Championship 2012 & 2014Masters 2025 & 2026McIlroy will win more green jacketsI would be shocked, shocked, if this is the final Masters win of Rory McIlroy’s career.He has unlocked his potential at Augusta National, and there are many more green jackets in his future. McIlroy in esteemed company Getty ImagesNick Faldo was part of the Sky Sports commentary team calling the winning moment and while the former Masters champion isn't always the most upbeat, he was full of praise for the Northern Irishman.Faldo knows only too well how hard it is to go back-to-back here. Here are the four men who have achieved a successful title defense at Augusta National:Jack Nicklaus (1965-66)Nick Faldo (1989-90)Tiger Woods (2001-02)Rory McIlroy (2025-2026)Who gives the defending champion their green jacket? When Rory McIlroy took a commanding six-shot lead heading into the weekend, a more pressing question than "will he win?" was "who will present him with his green jacket?" Last year's winner, of course, was himself.McIlroy lost that lead but rallied to win his second Masters, and we now have an answer to the second question as well: Augusta National Golf Club chairman Fred Ridley. Green jacket ceremony still to come!SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementFinal leaderboardAn entertaining week is over and Rory McIlroy was pushed all the way — here is how the top 10 shook out after four brilliant days at Augusta National.1. Rory McIlroy (-12)2. Scottie Scheffler (-11)T3. Tyrrell Hatton (-10)T3. Russell Henley (-10)T3. Justin Rose (-10)T3. Cameron Young (-10)T7. Collin Morikawa (-9)T7. Sam Burns (-9)T9. Max Homa (-8)T9. Xander Schauffele (-8)Not vintage McIlroy but he won't care Getty ImagesAs Brody says, it wasn't the prettiest golf from Rory McIlroy this week, but it was mighty effective.His did the bulk of his work on Friday, racing out to a record six-shot lead to bring into the weekend. That allowed him to be imperfect at the weekend and a 1-under 71 is enough for him to secure a second green jacket.Like London buses, one has brought two for McIlroy.Cue the celebrations across the United Kingdom as they salute one of their sporting heroes.Rory McIlroy just went back-to-back at the Masters while playing some of the messiest golf possible, and I happen to think that's awesome.McIlroy shares a moment with his familyHis mum and dad weren't here to see him win his first green jacket last year, but they weren't missing it for the world this time around!McIlroy hugs his daughter Poppy, kisses his wife Erica and then shares the warmest of warm embraces with his parents.There aren't the tears of last year, there are just smiles from ear to ear.What a moment.McIlroy successfully defends his Masters title! Getty ImagesHe's done it again — Rory McIlroy is the Masters champion for the second time in a row!After exorcising his demons here 12 months ago, the Northern Irishman has just become the fourth man to go back-to-back at Augusta National.Another historical week in this pocket of Georgia for McIlroy!SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementMcIlroy has a kick-in for the green jacket! Getty ImagesThe par putt won't go for McIlroy!But he has a kick-in for a second Masters title.He marks his ball and allows himself a huge smile to the gallery, where his family are waiting to greet him.But first, Cameron Young will finish his round.McIlroy safely onto the green!Having surveyed his lie, Rory McIlroy made light work of chipping the ball onto the green from the sand.It has left him 14 or 15 feet for par and remember, a bogey will be good enough for the green jacket.Surely even McIlroy can't find a way to snatch defeat from the jaws of victory here ...McIlroy into the bunker from the pine strawWisely, instead of going straight at the green via the direction of the fairway, Rory McIlroy opted for the more unorthodox shot over the leaderboard.It wasn't initially clear where his shot ended up, but it was into the front greenside bunker. It's not a great lie from there but he has three shots to get up and down.It is a very steep face on that bunker, though.As you might expect, McIlroy is taking plenty of time to look at his ball and the green.Plenty of trees between McIlroy and the greenRory McIlroy and caddy Harry Diamond trudge off into the foliage to find his ball, hoping and praying that he has a clear look at the green from there.He will have a clear swing at the ball but there are several trees between McIlroy and the green. They're all pretty slender, but I'm sure they look six feet wide for the defending champion.Having spent a few seconds looking at his lie, McIlroy is clearing the patrons out the way.Sublime or ridiculous, what have you got, Rory?A terrible tee shot from McIlroy on 18!Hold on, this isn't over yet.Rory McIlroy unintentionally faded his tee shot at 18 into the pine straw and, crucially, in amongst a selection of Augusta National's finest shrubbery. It doesn't quite look disastrous but it's certainly not what he will have wanted.Cameron Young did what his playing partner couldn't, sailing his drive straight a long way from any danger, though not down the middle of the fairway.SKIP ADVERTISEMENTAdvertisementRose secures top-five finish after agonizing back nine Getty ImagesWhat a roller coaster of a final round for Justin Rose.On the front nine, Rose transformed from middle-of-the-pack contender to the outright leader by two strokes. Rose made five birdies in that stretch and transfixed spectators with spectacular recovery shots and flawless putts.The back nine spelled disaster for Rose. He bogeyed three times, but some of his most bewildering misses came on pars that could have helped close the gap that opened between him and leader Rory McIlroy. Two of the worst miscues: a chip-in attempt in which Rose hit the ground before the ball on No. 12, and an errant 3-foot putt on No. 17 that forced him to take a bogey.The 45-year-old Rose had a chance to become the second-oldest winner of the Masters in his 21st appearance, but his brilliance to snatch the lead was nowhere to be found in the fateful back nine. He finished at 10 under and tied for third.Playing partner Jason Day made par on his final 11 holes of the tournament after a rough stretch to open the final round and closed at 5 under.McIlroy heads to 18 with a two-shot lead!No bother cleaning up from half a yard and Rory McIlroy is one hole away from defending his Masters title and he has a two-shot lead to Scottie Scheffler, who is in the clubhouse.Cameron Young had a good go at his long birdie putt on the 17th green but his rotten run on the green continues, leaving him three shots back heading to the 18th tee box.A bogey or better will give McIlroy his second green jacket — remember, he bogeyed this last year to take it to a playoff.Pitch perfect from McIlroy! Getty ImagesNerves, what nerves?A lovely chip onto the green and within a foot of the pin for another par putt that every patron left out there would be able to hole.He has just made a pretty tough shot look incredibly easy.McIlroy misses the green with his approachThere was one good swing for Rory McIlroy, nailing his drive into the heart of fairway but his approach deserted him.His ball clipped the front of the green but then dribbled to the right and onto the 'rough'. And that won't be an easy up and down for him given he is going to be straight at the pin as soon as that skips onto the green.A nervy moment for the defending champ who just needs to avoid dropping two shots on these final two holes.
